Available Hypothesis Quantities

Source: R/hypothesis-model-quantities.R
hypothesis_quantities.Rd

Lists the parameter names and aliases that hypothesis_BF() accepts for a fitted model, with the tests that it runs on each of them.

hypothesis_quantities(object, ...)

# Default S3 method
hypothesis_quantities(object, transform_scaled = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'BayesTools_fit'
hypothesis_quantities(object, transform_scaled = NULL, ...)

Arguments

object

a fitted model with a hypothesis_provider() method, for example a BayesTools_fit.

...

unused; unused arguments warn.

transform_scaled

whether the rendered statements test coefficients of scaled predictors on the original scale (TRUE) or the fitted scale (FALSE). The default NULL is the default of the provider (FALSE for a BayesTools_fit).

Value

A data frame with the columns alias (a name that hypothesis_BF() resolves to the row's quantity when the row's component is passed as the argument that selects the component of the model, which the provider names in its component_argument: the namespace argument for a BayesTools_fit; a name shared by several quantities of a component is not listed), parameter, component, term, bracket (a parameter[level] template for fitted factor terms, or a concrete level selector for each marginal-mean row), point_test, direction_test, contrast_test (NA for quantities without levels), point_test_methods, contrast_test_methods, and reason (the refusals of the rendered statements).

Details

The eligibility columns render the plans that hypothesis_BF_model() executes (see its details) for the statements <q> = <null> (point tests), <q> > <null> (directional and interval tests), and, for factor terms, <level> = <other level> (level contrasts) of every quantity q. The null value is 0; when 0 is a prior point mass, a support boundary without a regular prior ordinate, or outside the support (for example, a gated random-effect standard deviation or a variance proportion), the point test is rendered at an interior value of the support instead (the midpoint of a bounded support, one unit inside a half-bounded support, and 1 otherwise): point hypotheses at such values follow the per-value rules of hypothesis_BF_model(). A factor term lists the point-test methods available for all of its levels that the contrast does not fix, and the contrast-test methods available for all pairs of its levels. Region tests do not use a density method. The methods are the registered density backends that are advertised (hypothesis_density_backends(); the normal approximation is a rough check and is not listed).

See also

hypothesis_BF(), hypothesis_BF_model()
